text:
Elon Musk and Grimes found each other because they both independently made the same obscure joke about an AI thought experiment called Roko's Basilisk. Neither of them knew the other had made it. When they discovered the coincidence, Elon DM'd her. Their first real conversation lasted four hours.

Roko's Basilisk is a philosophical thought experiment about a future AI that punishes anyone who didn't help create it. It's the kind of idea that maybe a few thousand people on Earth find interesting, let alone funny. Elon had tweeted a joke about it. Grimes had made a music video referencing it. Neither one was aware of the other's version.

When someone pointed out the overlap, Elon messaged her. The conversation that followed wasn't flirting. It was two people discovering that their brains worked in the same strange way. AI, simulation theory, the future of consciousness, music as mathematics. Grimes later said she had never met anyone who could follow her thoughts at the speed she was thinking them.

Their first public appearance together was the 2018 Met Gala. They arrived together and the internet lost its mind because nobody could figure out how the richest man in tech and an experimental musician from Montreal ended up in the same universe.

The answer was simpler than anyone expected. They were both the kind of person who makes jokes about obscure AI philosophy at 2am and thinks that's normal. They didn't find each other through fame or fortune. They found each other through a thought experiment that maybe a thousand other people on Earth would have understood.

The rarest kind of connection isn't physical attraction. It's finding someone whose mind works like yours in a world that doesn't understand either of you.

We went all in on becoming a Video Factory back in September. 

We're on track to produce well over 100,000 videos over the next few quarters, likely much more.  

Sounds insane, but I'll explain why we're doing it and how: 

The why is easy: video absolutely crushes every other format in terms of engagement and performance.  Done well at scale it will have an enormous impact on your business. We know this because we're seeing it first hand.  

Personalized ads are where everyone's brain goes first, and yes we do that. 

In fact, when we switched from generic video ads to personalized ads our CTRs went from 1% to 15% overnight. 

That is reason enough alone for every company to become a video factory. 

But when the cost and effort of making a video gets cut by 98%, you start to realize, wow... we should use video for everything.  

So we built more. 

Now we make personalized videos for every single stage of the customer funnel: from our marketing team building an audience, to our CS team expanding an account. 

And we have seen funnel conversion improve at every stage as a result.

Our sales team has stopped making decks entirely. Video is just so much better. And now it's also easier. 

So how does one create a video factory? 

There are two paths: 

1) You can cobble together a solution with Claude. This involves glueing together a bunch of MCPs, APIs, skills,  and vibe-coded software that gives you an interface to make it work for everyone on the team. This can work for small teams, but breaks quickly at scale. It is also a pain in the ass to maintain because models are constantly getting better which means you need to constantly maintain and update your stack. Opus 5.5 is  great today, but not tomorrow.

quoted_tweet.author: Riley Brown
quoted_tweet.text:
The Fable of Clawd

A 2 minute 4K film made entirely in Blender, from one prompt on Fable 5.2. It took about 4.5 hours.

Claude built every asset in Blender by writing Python:
- 5 characters and props: Clawd, his friend Pip, a toy truck, a 3D-printed tulip and a gift box
- 7 full sets: a study, a staircase, a street, a workshop, an airport, a night sky and a house
- every camera move and every frame of animation across 52 shots

That came to 12,500 lines of code. It started 7 copies of itself to build the sets at the same time.

Then it rented 89 GPUs through RunPod to render 3,220 frames as fast as possible, 36 of them running at once. Total cost: a little over $20.

My biggest takeaway is my Claude Code knows it has access to cloud compute, so it's much more ambitious.

I tried a similar prompt on my other computer that doesn't have the runpod skill setup and it wasn't nearly as high quality

Full details linked below.

Robotics Data Is Becoming More Accessible PrismaXai

Training a robot requires more than collecting demonstrations. It requires understanding what actually happened during each task.

PrismaX recently showcased its Robotics Data Catalog at CoRL 2026, making real robot episodes easier to explore.

Each episode includes:

- Three synchronized camera views
- Task objectives and variations
- A dedicated quality score
- MP4 and MCAP data files

You can even preview the first 30 seconds before requesting access.

This is an important step toward making robotics data more transparent, organized, and useful for Physical AI development.

Better access to data means better opportunities to build and improve intelligent robots.

@PrismaXai

#PrismaX #Robotics #PhysicalAI

quoted_tweet.author: 𝙾𝙽𝚄 ♡
quoted_tweet.text:
From Real-World Demonstrations to Smarter Robots || @PrismaXai

A robot learning a task once is impressive.

A robot learning to adapt when the situation changes is a much bigger challenge.

That's what makes the collaboration between PrismaX and UPenn's GRASP Lab interesting.

By using PrismaX's YAM teleoperation data, researchers are exploring how real-world demonstrations can support robot learning through Reinforcement Learning.

The idea goes beyond simply teaching a robot what to do.

It's about helping robots become more adaptable when facing new tasks and unfamiliar environments.

What stands out to me is the role of real-world data in this process. Better learning doesn't come from algorithms alone. The quality of the experience behind them matters too.

The future of robotics depends not only on smarter models, but also on better ways to teach them.

#PrismaX #Robotics #PhysicalAI

quoted_tweet.text:
【说下circle和usdc的真实体感和投资价值】
身边很多深圳工作室老板朋友和大户都在定投 Circle，感觉多少都受了某饭影响。一个细小圈子很容易形成信息茧房。某一拨人靠类似的事情成功，就总想在别的领域复制：
1， 比如自己判断 BTC 四年周期做得成功，就把很大一部分仓位拿去玩美股
2，比如过去牛市里 MSTR 相对 BTC 有 Alpha，就线性推演未来Circle 相对 BTC 也有 Alpha

但我是真的在做加密支付，感受是USDC 在支付领域的真实 adoption，被圈内人严重高估了，虽然我不喜欢孙哥，但TRON的基本面好太多了。

几个关于稳定币支付的事实，大家可以去 check：

第一，现在推特上发言的加密 KOL 和用户，大多不是加密支付的主流群体。我们是稳定币的投资群体，不是消费群体。这些人会翻墙，也关注各种主流金融形式，手上都有信用卡。但凡有信用卡的人，基本不会用 U 付款，因为信用卡永远比 U 卡方便。

第二，整个加密 Web3 的支付机构，相比传统 PSP，有一个天然缺点，且没有传统 PSP 那种商户网络，他们作为稳定币兑法币的最后一站，可替代性非常强，而。这一点非常致命。最终形态大概率是成为传统支付商基建里的一环，而不是从后端去主宰、重塑整个行业链条。

第三，真正用稳定币支付的人，大部分在东南亚小国、非洲或南美。用户画像就两类：弱主权货币国家的小镇青年，以及灰产。他们往往只有钱包，可能没有交易所，大概率只认识TRON，基本上不持有metamask这类 EVM 钱包。

第四，关于usdc说几个反常识的数据。波场上流通的 USDT 大约 920 亿，以太坊大约 668 亿，波场多一些但你要明白tron上钱是以支付转账主导的，eth上是以defi投资生态主导的。从支付角度看，两者差距要大得多大得：2026 年，波场占稳定币支付金额约 66.6%，以太坊主网只有约 6.6%，差了 10 倍。即便把以太坊和它的 EVM 二层加在一起，也就十几个点，还是远被波场吊打。同期 USDT 贡献了约 84% 的支付金额，USDC 只有约 12%。

所以 USDC 在整个支付里的采用率，其实非常非常非常低。再加上波场的节点和商户深度绑定，它并不是短期内 L2 费用降低就能被取代的生态。波场现在比很多L2转账还贵，但大家仍然在用波场，不会换别的链。

基于这些，我对 USDC 作为稳定币支付基建、以及它的真实增长，是持保留态度的。

你说它会不会像 MSTR 一样，在牛市里相对 BTC 有 Alpha——牛市可能不看基本面，山寨起飞——那是另外一说，我不知道，一切皆有可能。

但如果你靠着 Circle 基本面给自己洗脑、动不动就 All in，来推导它会发展得很好，我并不认可。单从现在我对支付行业的体感，从基本面看，我觉得tron比 Circle 更牛逼。

我的感受是稳定币支付的底层是灰产，再说一遍，稳定币支付的底层是灰产
